'''Anthony Schuyler Arrott''' (April 1, 1928 – February 29, 2024) was an American-born Canadian physicist, and a professor at [[Carnegie Mellon University|Carnegie Institute of Technology]] and [[Simon Fraser University]]. He was a specialist in [[condensed matter physics]], the physics of [[magnetism]], and [[liquid crystal]]s. He was the author of over 200 scientific papers.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal|last=Goldfarb|first=R. B.|title=About the Cover|journal=[[IEEE Magnetics Letters]]|volume=7|pages=0000401|year=2016|doi=10.1109/LMAG.2016.2632141}}</ref> Arrott is the subject of the 2020 documentary ''Portrait,'' directed by Lily Ekimian and A.T. Ragheb.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Portrait|url=https://www.dogdoorfilms.com/feature-films/portrait|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706164935/https://www.dogdoorfilms.com/feature-films/portrait |archive-date=2020-07-06 |access-date=July 6, 2020|website=Dog Door Films}}</ref>

==Early work==
Arrott wrote his PhD thesis at the [[Carnegie Institute of Technology]] on the magnetic properties of Nickel alloys.<ref>{{cite thesis |first=Anthony |last=Arrott| title=DTIC AD0034763: The Magnetization of Some Alloys of Nickel and the Collective Electron Theory of Ferromagnetism | website=Internet Archive | date=1954-05-01 | url=https://archive.org/details/DTIC_AD0034763 | access-date=2023-07-15|type=PhD}}</ref>

After working at Carnegie Tech from 1953 to 1956, he joined the physics department of the [[Ford Motor Company|Ford]] Scientific Laboratory in [[Dearborn, Michigan]], where he studied the magnetic properties of iron alloys.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Goldfarb | first=Ron B. | title=About the Cover | journal=IEEE Magnetics Letters | publisher=Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) | volume=7 | year=2016 | issn=1949-307X | doi=10.1109/lmag.2016.2632141 | pages=C4}}</ref>

==Research area==
In 1957, he suggested a straightforward criterion for ferromagnetism from observations of magnetic isotherms.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |last=Arrott |first=A.
 |year=1957
 |title=Criterion for Ferromagnetism from Observations of Magnetic Isotherms
 |journal=[[Physical Review]]
 |volume=108 |issue=6 |pages=1394–1396
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.108.1394
|bibcode=1957PhRv..108.1394A
 }}</ref>
This method was called [[Arrott plot]]s.<ref>
{{cite book |last1=Aharoni |first1=A. |title=Introduction to the Theory of Ferromagnetism|pages=80–82|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2001|isbn=978-0-19-850809-0}}</ref><ref>
{{cite book |last1=du Trémolet de Lacheisserie |first1=E. |last2=Gignoux |first2=D. |last3=Schlenker |first3=M. |title=Magnetism (Fundamentals)|pages=133–137|publisher=Springer-Verlag New York|year=2005|isbn=978-0-387-22967-6}}
</ref>
In collaboration with Murray J. Press, he gave a description of surface singularities in liquid-crystal droplets.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |last1=Press |first1=M. J.
 |last2=Arrott |first2=A. S.
 |year=1974
 |title=Theory and Experiments on Configurations with Cylindrical Symmetry in Liquid-Crystal Droplets
 |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]
 |volume=33 |issue=7 |pages=403–406
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.33.403
|bibcode=1974PhRvL..33..403P
 }}</ref>
A lot of works are devoted to the properties of ferromagnetic samples (for example the so-called Arrott's cylinder<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hubert |first1=A. |last2=Schäfer |first2=R. |title=Magnetic Domains. The Analysis of Magnetic Microstructures|pages=161–163|publisher=Springer-Verlag Berlin|year=2009|isbn=978-3-540-64108-7}}</ref>) with micrometer and sub-micrometer sizes.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |last1=Arrott |first1=A.
 |last2=Heinrich |first2=B.
 |last3=Bloomberg |first3=D.
 |year=1974
 |title=Micromagnetics of magnetization processes in toroidal geometries
 |journal=[[IEEE Transactions on Magnetics]]
 |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=950–953
 |doi=10.1109/TMAG.1974.1058423
|bibcode=1974ITM....10..950A
 }}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
 |last1=Arrott |first1=A. S.
 |year=1977
 |title=Magnetization patterns with div M = 0
 |journal=[[Physica (journal)|Physica B+C]]
 |volume=86–88 |issue=3 |pages=1369–1370
 |doi=10.1016/0378-4363(77)90915-9
|bibcode=1977PhyBC..86.1369A
 }}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal|last=Arrott|first=A. S.|title=Visualization and Interpretation of Magnetic Configurations Using Magnetic Charge|journal=[[IEEE Magnetics Letters]]|volume=7|pages=1108505|year=2016|doi=10.1109/LMAG.2016.2631127|s2cid=31450506}}
</ref> Commissioned in 1978, Arrott designed the Thermal Neutron Facility at the [[TRIUMF]] cyclotron.<ref name=":0" />

==Death==
Arrott died in [[Burnaby]], [[British Columbia]], Canada on February 29, 2024, at the age of 95.<ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam |url=https://www.sfu.ca/retirees/in-memoriam/a_g.html |website=Simon Fraser University |access-date=4 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IEEE Magnetics Newsletter, Volume 64 |url=https://ieeemagnetics.org/files/ieeemagnetics/2024-05/IEEE%20MagSoc%20Newsletter%20Vol.64-1-Mar2024-PDF-revised.pdf |website=IEEE Magnetics |access-date=4 February 2025 |pages=12}}</ref> He was preceded in death by his wife Patricia in 2016, she was a notable visual artist.<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 11, 1954 |title=Carnegie Tech To Graduate 772 Students |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/pittsburgh-sun-telegraph-carnegie-tech-t/168079373/ |access-date=2025-03-16 |work=Pittsburgh Sun-Telegraph |pages=17 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> 

Arrott and his wife's artwork were subject of a documentary film, ''Portrait'' (2020) directed by Ahmed T. Ragheb, and Lily Ekimian Ragheb of Studio Ragheb.

==Recognition==
*1951: Allis-Chalmers Fellowship in Magnetism
*1963: [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1963|Guggenheim Fellowship in Physics]]
*1982: Gold Medal for Physical Sciences from the Science Council of British Columbia
*1986: Medal for Lifetime Achievement in Physics from the [[Canadian Association of Physicists]]
